claims.text: Severe plastic deformation with in-situ high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction will improve phase stability in coarse polycrystalline metallic alloys.
Severe plastic deformation with in-situ high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction will refine the microstructure of coarse polycrystalline metallic alloys.
Severe plastic deformation with in-situ high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction will optimize alloy properties relative to conventional processing.
The proposed processing temperature is approximately 300°C.
The proposed controlled strain rate is approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The proposed severe-plastic-deformation treatment uses cyclic loading.
Processing at 300°C with controlled strain rate and cyclic loading enables sufficient diffusion.
Processing at 300°C with controlled strain rate and cyclic loading enables sufficient dislocation activity.
Dynamic phase evolution occurs during the proposed deformation treatment.
Grain refinement occurs during the proposed deformation treatment.
In-situ high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction can capture phase transformations in real time.
In-situ high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction can capture grain-size evolution in real time.
Simultaneous diffraction measurements under severe deformation directly link microstructural changes with property enhancements.
The proposed method will increase mechanical strength.
The proposed method will improve toughness.
The proposed method may improve corrosion resistance.
Conventional heat treatments and typical mechanical processing target only one aspect at a time.
Conventional processing does not provide real-time insight into dynamic microstructural evolution.
The method is expected to be effective under moderate-temperature severe-plastic-deformation conditions.
Results may differ under extreme processing conditions outside the specified regime.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats in-situ X-ray diffraction as part of a method that improves material structure and properties, whereas the mechanism describes diffraction only as a monitoring tool. No causal account explains how measurement by X-rays itself produces the asserted improvements, as distinct from severe plastic deformation.
